{{Achievement|So what is the chessboard problem you ask? Well, let me tell you. The problems appear in many myths and legends about the history and creation of chess. The first know recording of the problem is from 1256 by the Islamic scholar Ibn Khallikan. The story revolves around the inventor of chess, in some versions of the story the role is played by Sissa a mythological creature from India known for the invention of Chaturanga, a predecessor to Chess. In other versions of the main protagonist might is a mathematician, a minister, or in some a stranger or someone of poor decent like a farmer. The story often has a ruler of some sort approach the protagonist and ask them to entertain them with a new game. The inventor presents their ruler with the game of chess and the ruler asks the inventor for his price. The inventor ponders this ask for a simple offering based on his creation. A single grain of rice or some versions say wheat, on the first square and double that amount on the second square and double that amount on the third square and so one for the sixty-four squares of the chessboard. The ruler laughs at the meager price and accepts but his court treasurer tells him that the staggering about of rice, or wheat, needed to fill the board in this manner. The total would be eighteen quintillions, four hundred forty-six quadrillion, seven hundred forty-four trillion, seventy-three billion, seven hundred nine million, five hundred fifty-one thousand, six hundred and fifteen, over one point four trillion metric tons. Or put simply which is over two thousand times the annual world production of wheat, which in the period twenty-twenty to twenty-twenty-one was an estimated about seven hundred seventy-three million metric tones. Anyway, the stories do differ and this point. Some say that the inventor gets offered a nice position as a high-ranking advisor and in other versions, he gets executed. Now there is probably a moral here but low and behold I am out of character. One could say that is the definition of irony, isn't it?||}}

|-|Trivia=
*'''No Gnome Left Behind''' is a reference to the [[w:c:half-life:Garden Gnome|Garden]] [[w:c:left4dead:Gnome Chompski|Gnome]] from the Half Life and Left 4 Dead games. The gnome has to be carried through the entire mission to the final location in all 3 games.
*'''For The Mad Hatter''' is a reference to {{w|Hatter (Alice's Adventures in Wonderland)|The Mad Hatter}} from {{w|Lewis Carroll}}'s 1865 book {{w|Alice's Adventures in Wonderland}}, who is frozen in time forever stuck at 6pm in an endless tea party. The Hatter tried to sing to the foul-tempered {{w|Queen of Hearts (Alice's Adventures in Wonderland)|Queen of Hearts}} who sentenced him to death by decapitation. Father Time retaliated and froze The Mad Hatter in time out of respect for him. The "Laohu Dashi" outfit is a reference to {{w|Bruce Lee}} and his yellow jumpsuit. The name translates to "Tiger Master", referencing the black and yellow colors of the outfit.
